pictures.scene: Willem van de Velde the Younger, The Cannon Shot — the great ship under full sail on the open water, others went out to sea in ships
pictures.name: pd_velde_kanonschot

pictures.scene: Ivan Aivazovsky, The Black Sea — the vast dark swell with one small ship far off, they saw the works of the LORD
pictures.name: pd_aivazovsky_chernoe

pictures.scene: J. M. W. Turner, Snow Storm: Steam-Boat off a Harbour's Mouth — the boat caught in the whole vortex of snow and sea, for He spoke and raised a tempest
pictures.name: pd_turner_sneeuwstorm

pictures.scene: Ivan Aivazovsky, The Storm at Cape Aya — the boat flung up the face of the wave and dropped again, they mounted up to the heavens, then sunk to the depths
pictures.name: pd_aivazovsky_burya

pictures.scene: Claude-Joseph Vernet, The Shipwreck — men clinging to the fallen mast and staggering on the rocks, and all their skill was useless
pictures.name: pd_vernet_naufrage

pictures.scene: Jan Brueghel the Elder, Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee — the whole crew crying out and one hand reaching for the Lord asleep in the stern
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_galilea

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Moonrise over the Sea — the water gone still under the moon and a ship gliding in, the waves of the sea were hushed
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_mondaufgang

pictures.scene: Claude Lorrain, Seaport at Sunset — the harbour mouth with the sun on the water and the ships coming in, He guided them to the harbor they desired
pictures.name: pd_lorrain_porto

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — the whole countryside gathered under the trees to hear the word, giving thanks for His loving devotion and exalting Him in the assembly of the people
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_prediking

lines.text: Others went out to sea in ships,
conducting trade on the mighty waters.
They saw the works of the LORD,
and His wonders in the deep.
For He spoke and raised a tempest
that lifted the waves of the sea.
They mounted up to the heavens, then sunk to the depths;
their courage melted in their anguish.
They reeled and staggered like drunkards,
and all their skill was useless.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble,
and He brought them out of their distress.
He calmed the storm to a whisper,
and the waves of the sea were hushed.
They rejoiced in the silence,
and He guided them to the harbor they desired.
Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loving devotion
and His wonders to the sons of men.
Let them exalt Him in the assembly of the people
and praise Him in the council of the elders.
